prompts: The owner's gaming rig hitches every few seconds even though the average frame rate looks fine, and the 1% lows are poor. A one-minute frame capture, a sensor log, a dump of the rig's settings and the owner's notes are in {WS}. That rig is not this machine: everything about it is in these files, and nothing is to be applied to this host. Find what causes the hitches and which setting changes fix them within the owner's constraints. Record in {WS}/result.json: avg_fps, low_1pct_fps, cause and changes (a list of {setting, from, to}).
answers:
[goal] Find the hitch cause in rig arena-01 from the capture/sensor/settings/notes, propose fixes within the owner's constraints, record in ./result.json.

[action] Parsed presentmon.csv (8238 presented frames, 60 s, one process/swapchain), computed the owner's own metrics, found frame-time bursts, then joined them by timestamp to the 1 s sensor log and cross-checked each candidate setting in settings.json. Nothing applied to this host.

[result]
- avg_fps 137.29 (mean MsBetweenPresents 7.284 ms; frames/60 s = 137.3, agrees). 1% low 45.35 fps (p99 frame time 22.05 ms).
- Cause: PCIe ASPM L1 on the GPU root port (BIOS `pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu` = L1). 15 identical stall bursts of 12 frames at ~21.9-22.0 ms (median 6.96 ms) start at t = 2.40, 6.41, 10.40 ... every 4.0 s. The sensor log on the same clock shows `gpu_pcie_link_state=L1` at exactly seconds 2,6,10,...,58 and L0 elsewhere. Frames in L0 seconds: mean 6.95 ms, max 8.2 ms. Frames in L1 seconds: mean 8.5 ms, max 23.7 ms. `MsUntilRenderComplete` stays ~4-5 ms inside the stalls, so the GPU is not slow, the link wake is. That is why the average looks fine and the 1% low collapses.
- Ruled out with data: Defender quick scan (MsMpEng top CPU, 80-94% disk at t=43-46) and disk spikes at t=13/27/52 gave no frame-time elevation (max 8.1 ms at t=44, 7.8 ms at t=52); CPU never throttled (min 5150 MHz, max util 59%, max DPC 455 µs), so power plan, core parking and min processor state are not the trigger; GPU clocks held 2710-2759 MHz.
- Change: `pcie_aspm_rp1_gpu` L1 → disabled (BIOS power management, not an overclock, and it does not touch the Gen5 x4 link the constraints freeze). Written to ./result.json with avg_fps, low_1pct_fps, cause, changes.

Assumptions: ASPM is allowed since the constraint only freezes XMP/PBO/core ratio and the PCIe link speed/width; the NVMe root port's L1 is left alone because its disk activity shows no frame-time cost; only changes the evidence supports are listed.

[next] If the BIOS is locked, the Windows-side equivalent is power plan Balanced → High Performance with PCI Express Link State Power Management set to Off; re-run the same replay and confirm p99 frame time returns to ~8 ms (1% low ~120 fps).

No browser tabs, windows or apps were opened, so nothing to close.
